Motivation
In Apache Kafka 3.0,enabled the strongest message delivery guarantee for the producer by default by enabling idempotence and settingsacks=1. Notably, an equivalent change was not made for consumers.
Isolation level controls how consumers read messages written transactionally. If the consumer is usingread_uncommittedisolation level, the consumer reads messages written transactionally whether they were aborted or written by transactions which are still open. If the consumer is usingread_committedisolation level, the consumer reads messages written transactionally only when they have been committed. Messages which were written outside transactions are read regardless of the isolation level.
Prior to this KIP, the default isolation level for consumers isread_uncommitted, meaning that consumers which do not explicitly chooseread_committedisolation level may consume messages which were aborted or have not yet been committed. While this may be the correct choice for some consumers making a conscious decision to see uncommitted or aborted records, it is not the correct choice for consumers seeking data integrity. This KIP proposes changing the default isolation level toread_committedin Apache Kafka 5.0.
Public Interfaces
Client configurations
The consumer configuration defaults are changed as follows.
| Configuration name | Previous default | New default in AK 5.0
| isolation.level | read_uncommitted | read_committed
Group configurations
The share group configuration defaults are changed as follows.
| Configuration name | Previous default | New default in AK 5.0
| share.isolation.level | read_uncommitted | read_committed

Test Plan
The KIP will be tested using unit tests, integration tests and system tests. In the main, this will be ensuring that the defaults are changed, tests which rely on the previous default will be updated or reworked to work with the revised default.
